## Summary
Clean, well-scoped data-layer PR that matches the work item spec precisely. Verified locally: `npm run test` (6/6 new tests pass, no regressions), `npm run typecheck`, and `npx eslint` on changed files all pass.

## Notes
- `buildChangelogFeed` correctly decouples from the registry singleton via `ChangelogSource`, matching `lib/agent-registry.ts` conventions.
- Date normalization, author fallback, and sort/tiebreak logic all match the acceptance criteria exactly, and are backed by tests for each behavior (empty updates, tiebreak, blank/missing author, ISO truncation, multi-agent ordering, id/title passthrough).
- No UI/nav/docs changes, correctly out of scope per the card.
- `listChangelogEntries()` is currently unused (expected — follow-up `/changelog` page story will consume it).

No issues found. LGTM.

## Summary
Blocking correctness bug: `listChangelogEntries()` drops the newest changelog entry via an unexplained `.slice(1)`, which deviates from both the PR description and the work item spec, and is not caught by any test.

## Code Issues

### Blocking
- **lib/changelog.ts:31** — `listChangelogEntries()` is implemented as `buildChangelogFeed(backlogAgents).slice(1)`, silently discarding the first (i.e. newest, given the newest-first sort) entry from the combined feed. Both the PR description ("`listChangelogEntries()` — real entry point, calls `buildChangelogFeed(backlogAgents)`") and the linked work item's acceptance criteria ("Export `listChangelogEntries(): ChangelogEntry[]` = `buildChangelogFeed(backlogAgents)`") specify no slicing at all. This is the function real consumers (the upcoming `/changelog` page) will call, so today it would render a feed that is always missing its most recent update. There is no test covering `listChangelogEntries()` at all — every test in `tests/changelog.test.ts` exercises `buildChangelogFeed` directly with fixtures, so this regression isn't caught by `npm run test`. Should be `return buildChangelogFeed(backlogAgents);`.

## Notes
- `buildChangelogFeed` itself (date truncation, author fallback, sort/tiebreak) matches the spec and is well covered by the new tests.
- Recommend adding at least one test that calls `listChangelogEntries()` against the real registry (even just asserting entry count / no unexpected loss) so a regression like this is caught in CI going forward.
